instruct:
A female voice. Accent: A 1930s American woman in her early thirties. Husky, slightly raspy alto with a hint of nasal brightness. Speaks quickly and crisply, with a dry, wisecracking, working-girl edge. Her voice is a little unstable: on emotional or surprised words it cracks upward into a brief, high squeak, then drops back to the husky register. Tough on the surface, vulnerable underneath. Clear mid-Atlantic-leaning diction, not breathy or sultry.
. Mary Smith in the film Easy Living.
Natural, conversational telephone speech, 1950s.
sample_text: Look, mister, I work for a living. I ride the bus and I eat at the automat, and nobody ever gave me anything before.
